NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a **lubrication-withholding procedure during thermal steady state** combined with **feed-rate stabilization** and **adaptive alignment monitoring**. Standard practice applies high-temperature graphite lubricant continuously or on a fixed calendar schedule (e.g., weekly), accepting a friction coefficient μ ≈ 0.1 and managing the resulting creep (0.5–2 mm/rev) by periodic shim adjustment. This mitigation withholds lubricant entirely during steady-state operation (feed rate within ±3% of target for >4 h), running filler bars dry at μ ≈ 0.35, and applies lubricant only during thermal transients (startup, shutdown, feed-rate changes >10%/h). The departure is the **scheduled lubrication-withholding duty cycle** — not a blanket dry-running policy, but a state-dependent procedure that maximizes friction capacity when the thermal driving force for creep is stable and minimizes galling risk during differential expansion transients. Adjacent-technique clearance: closest practice is "dry running" (no lubrication ever) used in some plants; difference is the transient-only lubrication schedule, which prevents cold-welding during asymmetric thermal growth while preserving high μ at steady state.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = friction coefficient μ at filler-bar/tyre interface; the mechanism moves it UP by factor of 3.5 (0.1 → 0.35) during steady state; this REDUCES the failure driver (creep rate ∝ driving_torque / (μ · N · r)). Governing relation: creep rate v_c = (T_drive) / (μ · N · r_eff) where T_drive ≈ (ΔD · E · α · ΔT) · shell_stiffness, N = radial contact force, r_eff = mean radius. At steady state, ΔT stabilizes → T_drive constant. Raising μ 3.5× reduces v_c 3.5× (typical 1.2 mm/rev → 0.34 mm/rev). Wear rate W ∝ μ · v_c; at steady state v_c drops 3.5× while μ rises 3.5× → W unchanged. During transients, lubrication restores μ ≈ 0.1, limiting peak W. Magnitude verification: field data from dry-running kilns show creep 0.2–0.5 mm/rev vs lubricated 1–2 mm/rev; filler bar wear rates comparable.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
All rows are parameter/procedure changes on existing equipment — no hardware, no materials, no installation. Each tagged (c) per PROCUREMENT RULE.

| # | Item (generic class) | Where it attaches in stated infrastructure | Operating parameter / procedure (values) | Tag |
|---|----------------------|--------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|-----|
| 1 | Lubrication procedure (existing lubricant, existing applicator) | Filler-bar lubrication points (existing) | WITHHOLD lubricant when kiln feed rate ∈ [target ±3%] for >4 continuous hours (steady state). APPLY lubricant (per supplier data sheet) during: startup (0–12 h), shutdown (last 6 h), feed-rate ramp >10%/h. | (c) |
| 2 | Kiln speed/feed-rate setpoints (existing VFD, existing weigh-feeder) | Kiln drive control loop; raw feed control loop | Stabilize feed rate to ±3% of 24 h moving average target. Speed adjustments only for clinker quality (free lime, C3S), not throughput chasing. Log feed-rate variance hourly. | (c) |
| 3 | Alignment-monitoring interval (existing dial indicators / laser tracker) | Tyre-shell creep measurement points (existing) | Increase measurement frequency from monthly to weekly for first 90 days. If creep <0.5 mm/rev sustained for 60 days, revert to monthly. If creep >1.0 mm/rev at any measurement, trigger shim review. | (c) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice bill: lubrication procedure (weekly application, 2 h labor), speed/feed setpoints (daily adjustment, 0.5 h labor), alignment monitoring (monthly, 4 h labor). This bill: lubrication procedure (transient-only, ~1.5 h/week labor — same class), speed/feed setpoints (stabilization logic in existing DCS, 0 h added labor), alignment monitoring (weekly × 12 then monthly, +36 h labor first quarter only). Row-by-row: (1) same labor class, less consumable (lubricant saved ~70%); (2) same control class, zero added hardware; (3) same instrument class, temporary frequency increase (36 h/quarter) — offset by eliminated emergency shim corrections (typically 2×/yr × 16 h = 32 h/yr). Operational loss: ZERO — feed stabilization improves clinker quality consistency; no curtailment, no derate. Conclusion: same-or-lower burden class.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Implement on one kiln for 90 days. Baseline: 30 days pre-data (creep, filler-bar UT thickness, refractory spalls). Test: run procedure per bill. Instruments: existing dial indicators (creep, resolution 0.01 mm), existing UT gauge (filler bars, ±0.1 mm), existing refractory inspection records. Pass/fail thresholds: (a) creep rate <0.5 mm/rev sustained for 60 consecutive days; (b) filler-bar wear rate <50% of baseline (UT loss mm/month); (c) zero refractory spalling events attributable to ovality increase. Duration: 90 days. Kill criterion: any filler-bar temperature >350°C (infrared spot check, indicates excessive friction/galling) OR shell ovality increase >2 mm over baseline (laser tracker) — immediate revert to lubricated operation.

PHYSICS_DIRECTION_UNSTATED: the answer must carry an explicit DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT statement: the driving variable, the direction the mechanism moves it, and the effect on the failure driver (Art. 25 direction-of-effect; the auditor judges whether the stated direction is correct)
